_doc: Single source of truth shared by mechanical/puck.py and hardware/gen_pcb.py. Units mm. Board coordinates: origin on the puck axis, +x right, +y up, viewed from the cap (top). z = 0 at the face that seats on the Avalon weight.

puck.insert: M1.6 heat-set brass insert, OD 2.4, L 3.0

_pcb_dia: Puck OD = Avalon barebow weight OD (40 mm). Cavity 37 mm (cap_wall 1.5) minus 0.5 mm clearance per side.

bosses._angles: 40 deg keeps the boss face on the board beside the cell notch and 1.4 mm from the cell, 148 deg keeps it out of the module's antenna keep-out.

cell.part: Varta CP1654 A3 (wire or tag version, hand-soldered, never reflowed)
cell._swell: Varta drawing: max 7.0 mm including cell deflection (1.5 mm free space for abuse conditions). A soft foam pad may fill the gap.
cell._pcb_hole: The cell sits in a notch in the PCB that is open to the rim, on the insulator over the base (saves the 0.8 mm board). The relief (a circle of radius r bulging depth mm past the notch edge, on the + pad side) lets the bottom (+ can) tab or wire bend up onto the + pad.

connector.part: Samzo PR5L4015-2P-C-F magnetic receptacle (Electrokit 41035992); cable side PR5L5015-2P-C-H (Electrokit 41035991)
connector._note: Samzo drawing GZ0254-P001. Mounted on the PCB; the cap has a chimney down to the connector top so the plug reaches it. mass_g is an estimate: weigh the part.

trim._note: Positions and lengths are solved by puck.py (1-2 pins) to put the centre of mass on the axis. Optional: the cap always has the pockets; without pins the puck works, only ~1 mm off-balance. Brass, not steel: steel is pulled by the connector magnets.
